output.brief:
The 26-point gap mostly reflects who gets into Bridge Hours, not what the program does. Participants started far lower in the fall: a mean of 182.8 against 215.1, and 91% were below the 40th percentile. Among students with similar fall scores, winter results and growth are almost the same for participants and non-participants. The remaining differences are under one point and go in both directions. So the dashboard doesn't show harm. Northgate's "faster growth" claim doesn't show benefit either. Low scorers grow faster whether or not they are tutored. The comparison can't detect a small effect in either direction. I'm fairly sure of this (about 85–90%). What I don't know is whether the program helps, or whether the method conflict a teacher reported lowers scores.

What to do:
- Don't cut the contract on the raw gap, and don't expand it yet.
- Have the research office present the like-for-like comparison to the board in place of the raw chart. The comparison of students just either side of the 196 cut is due 27 Feb.
- Have the math coordinator observe sessions and check the fraction lessons against the classroom sequence.
- Keep the referral list. Opening sign-up would make later comparisons less clear.
- Consider a short renewal or conditional decision until effectiveness data is available.
